skill_drafts.name: Install Third-Party JAR to Local Repository
skill_drafts.description: Procedure to add external JAR files into the local Maven repository for project dependency resolution. Use when integrating non-standard or proprietary libraries that are not available in remote repositories.
skill_drafts.objective: Register external JAR artifact in local repository
applicable_signals: Build failure due to missing artifact in Central Repository
Requirement to use offline or air-gapped dependency
Integration of vendor-supplied or custom JAR
contraindications: Artifact already available in Central Repository
Artifact should be deployed to shared remote repository for team access
Dependency is managed by a corporate artifact repository
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify JAR metadata', 'detail': 'Determine group ID, artifact ID, version, and packaging type (jar) for the third-party library.'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Execute install:install-file goal', 'detail': 'Run Maven install:install-file with -Dfile, -DgroupId, -DartifactId, -Dversion, and -Dpackaging parameters.'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Verify local repository indexing', 'detail': 'Confirm the JAR appears in the local repository directory structure (typically ~/.m2/repository).'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Declare dependency in pom.xml', 'detail': 'Add a <dependency> block with matching group ID, artifact ID, and version to the project pom.xml.'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Test build resolution', 'detail': 'Run mvn clean compile or mvn dependency:resolve to confirm the dependency is resolved from local repository.'}
triggers: Third-party JAR unavailable in remote repositories
Local-only dependency required for project build
Proprietary or non-standard library integration needed
constraints: JAR file must be physically available locally
Group ID, artifact ID, and version must be known or inferred
Local repository must have write permissions
cautions: Local-only installation does not share the dependency with team members; consider remote deployment for shared use.
Verify JAR integrity and source before installation to avoid security risks.
output_contract: JAR file indexed in local repository; project build resolves dependency without download attempts; dependency declaration in pom.xml matches installed artifact metadata.

metadata.prompt:
To install a third-party JAR to the local Maven repository:
1. Obtain the JAR file and identify its group ID, artifact ID, and version.
2. Use the Maven install:install-file goal to register the JAR in the local repository.
3. Verify the JAR is indexed and accessible to the project build.
4. Update project pom.xml with the corresponding dependency declaration.
5. Run a test build to confirm the dependency resolves without download attempts.

skill_drafts.name: Deploy Third-Party JAR to Remote Repository
skill_drafts.description: Procedure to publish external JAR files to a shared remote Maven repository for team-wide access. Use when making proprietary or third-party libraries available across multiple projects or developers.
skill_drafts.objective: Publish external JAR artifact to shared remote repository
applicable_signals: Artifact not available in Central Repository
contraindications: Artifact already published in Central Repository
No remote repository access or credentials available
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Verify artifact coordinates', 'detail': 'Confirm groupId, artifactId, and version are defined and follow naming conventions'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure repository credentials', 'detail': 'Set up authentication in Maven settings.xml or equivalent for target remote repository'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Execute deployment', 'detail': 'Use Maven deploy command or repository management tool to publish JAR to remote repository'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify accessibility', 'detail': 'Confirm artifact is resolvable by dependent projects via dependency declaration'}
triggers: Third-party JAR must be shared across team
Multiple projects need access to same external library
constraints: Remote repository must be accessible and authenticated
Artifact must have valid Maven coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version)
Deployment credentials must be configured in settings.xml or equivalent
cautions: Verify artifact licensing before deploying to shared repository
Ensure version numbering follows team conventions to avoid conflicts
Test artifact resolution from dependent projects after deployment
Document repository location and access requirements for team
output_contract: JAR artifact published to remote repository and accessible to all team members via dependency declaration. Artifact is discoverable and resolvable by Maven dependency resolution.

metadata.prompt: Deploy a third-party JAR artifact to a shared remote Maven repository. Ensure the artifact is properly configured with coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version) and that authentication credentials are set up for the target repository. Verify that all team members can resolve the artifact via dependency declaration after deployment.

skill_drafts.name: Configure Multiple Repository Sources
skill_drafts.description: Setup and management of multiple Maven repositories (local, remote, mirrors, proxies) to resolve dependencies from diverse sources. Establishes a multi-source dependency resolution strategy when projects require artifacts from multiple repository endpoints or need fallback resolution paths.
applicable_signals: Build fails with artifact not found from single repository
Need to route requests through proxy or mirror
Requirement to balance load across multiple repository endpoints
Security or access control requires repository selection logic
contraindications: Single repository is sufficient for all project dependencies
No network constraints or failover requirements
No security or access control requirements
Build environment has no external repository access
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Define multiple repository endpoints', 'detail': 'Add repository entries to Maven settings or POM with distinct IDs, URLs, and optional authentication credentials'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure repository priority and fallback order', 'detail': 'Establish the sequence in which Maven will attempt to resolve artifacts from each repository'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Apply mirror rules if needed', 'detail': 'Define mirror mappings to route requests for specific repositories through a mirror or proxy endpoint'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Configure proxy settings if required', 'detail': 'Set proxy host, port, and authentication for outbound repository access'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Validate configuration', 'detail': 'Run a test build to confirm dependencies resolve from appropriate sources and no circular references exist'}
triggers: Repository failover or load distribution needed
Project dependencies span multiple remote repositories
constraints: Repository endpoints must be reachable and properly authenticated
Mirror and proxy configurations must not create circular references
Repository priority order must be explicitly defined to avoid ambiguity
Credentials for authenticated repositories must be securely stored
cautions: Misconfigured mirrors can cause dependency resolution failures
Proxy timeouts may require tuning for slow network conditions
Repository priority order affects build reproducibility; document rationale
Ensure mirror rules do not inadvertently block access to required repositories
output_contract: Maven settings configured with multiple repository endpoints; build successfully resolves dependencies from appropriate sources in priority order; no unresolved artifact errors; proxy and mirror rules function without circular references

metadata.prompt: Configure Maven settings to enable dependency resolution from multiple repository sources. Define repository endpoints, apply mirror rules, configure proxy settings, and establish priority order for artifact lookup. Verify that the build resolves dependencies from appropriate sources according to configuration.

skill_drafts.name: Secure Remote Repository Access via Authenticated HTTPS
skill_drafts.description: Configuration of credentials and HTTPS authentication for accessing remote Maven repositories with security requirements. Enforces encrypted transport and credential protection when repositories require authentication.
skill_drafts.objective: Enforce secure authenticated access to remote repositories
contraindications: Public unauthenticated repository without credential requirements
HTTP-only repository where encryption is not enforced
workflow_steps: Verify repository URL uses HTTPS protocol
Obtain and securely store authentication credentials
Configure credentials in secure credential store or encrypted settings
Establish HTTPS connection to remote repository
Validate certificate and authenticate with provided credentials
Test dependency resolution through authenticated HTTPS channel
Confirm build succeeds with secure artifact access
triggers: HTTPS encryption is mandatory for repository access
Sensitive credentials must be protected during artifact resolution
constraints: HTTPS connection must be established before credential transmission
Credentials must not be stored in plaintext in configuration files
Certificate validation must be enabled for HTTPS connections
cautions: Verify certificate chain validity to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks
Rotate credentials regularly and revoke compromised tokens
Audit credential access and repository connection logs
output_contract: Remote repository access configured with valid credentials; HTTPS connection established and verified; build resolves dependencies securely through encrypted transport; no plaintext credentials exposed in logs or configuration.

metadata.prompt: Configure HTTPS authentication for remote repository access. Establish secure credentials, validate HTTPS connection, and verify dependency resolution through encrypted channel. Ensure credentials are stored securely and transport is encrypted.
